settings.title: Settings
settings.lede: Most of these map to a flag the engine already has, so anything you set here you can also pass on a command line. Privacy is the exception: it states what the window sends rather than setting anything.
settings.developerDesc: Keeps package, build and test-runner caches that were used inside the idle window, instead of clearing them completely.
settings.developerHeldNone: Nothing is being held back – every cache is offered in full.
settings.idleDesc: A file untouched for longer than this counts as stale. The newest of its write, access and creation times is what is measured.
settings.tempDesc: A shorter window for %TEMP% and the Windows temp folders, which turn over much faster.
settings.largeDesc: What section 19 counts as large enough to offer you.
settings.scheduleDesc: A Windows Scheduled Task that runs the safe batch, notifies you, and never touches an interactive section.
settings.scheduleConseq: Maps to --install-task, which refuses under npx because that cache is evicted.
settings.versionNote: The desktop app bundles the engine it was built against, so the two can never disagree about what a section does.
settings.promoNote: These are the team’s own tools, not an advertising network – nothing here is sold, tracked or third-party, and windowsweep never appears in its own list.
settings.noKeys: No destination is configured in this build, so nothing is actually sent from it.
settings.about: windowsweep reclaims disk space on Windows. It names every path before it touches one, and refuses your documents, credentials and browser state outright. The desktop window drives the same engine the command-line tool runs.
history.title: History
history.lede: Every run made in this window, and a summary of runs from your other machines if you are signed in.
history.chartNote: the frame does not move with the data
history.chartAria_one: Bytes freed by the last run
history.chartAria_other: Bytes freed by each of the last {{count}} runs
history.chartEmpty: No real run has finished in this window yet.
history.cloudNoReport: The full report stays on the machine that made it.
history.emptyBody: No run has finished in this window yet. A dry-run costs nothing and deletes nothing.
history.emptyDryBody: A dry-run costs nothing and deletes nothing.
history.cloudEmptyTitle: No run summaries from other machines
history.cloudEmptyBody: When a run finishes in the desktop app on another machine signed in as you, its summary appears here.
history.cloudEmptyBodySignedOut: Sign in and your other machines’ run summaries appear here. Nothing syncs while you are signed out.
history.budgetNote: Twenty at a time with a cursor, never the whole table – the same budget the engine itself keeps.
report.emptyBody: A report is written for every run, including a dry-run, and the file on disk says exactly what this screen says.
report.notFound: That run is no longer in this window’s history.
report.exportDone: Markdown and HTML come from the engine’s own --export, not from this window – so an exported report and this page cannot drift apart.
report.barsAria: Bytes freed by each section in this run
report.barsAriaDryRun: Bytes each section would free in this dry-run
report.whereSummary: Where this file lives, and what else reads it
report.whereBody: Written to <1>{{path}}</1> by the engine itself, in schema 1. This window renders that file – it does not compute anything of its own, which is why a report opened here and a report opened in a text editor can never disagree.
report.whereExport: The same file is what <1>--export md</1> and <3>--export html</3> convert, and what an agent reads when it drives windowsweep from a script.
report.fileMissing: No report file was found for this run, so only its summary is shown.
report.fileFailed: This run’s report file could not be read, so only its summary is shown.
account.title: Sign in only if you want your settings on another machine.
account.lede: Reclaiming space is <1>never gated</1>. Signing in moves your settings and a summary of each run between your own machines, and that is all it does.
account.cardBody: You are using every feature windowsweep has. Signing in adds one thing: your settings and a summary of each run follow you to another machine.
account.browserNote: It opens your normal browser, not a window inside this app – so you can see the address bar and windowsweep never sees your password.
account.stored.settings.why: So a second machine starts where you left off.
account.stored.runs.why: Nine fields per run: the date, the mode, whether it was a dry-run, whether it was elevated, which section numbers ran, the bytes reclaimed, the bytes a dry-run estimated, how long it took, and an id.
account.stored.lastSeen.why: A timestamp, refreshed when this window syncs, so a machine you no longer use is recognisable as such.
account.neverStored: <1>Never stored:</1> a file path, a folder name, a drive label, your machine name or your Windows user name. A cloud run row is labelled <3>summary only</3> in History for exactly that reason – the detail stays on the machine that made it.
account.sync.never: Never uploaded, signed in or not
account.sync.runsUploaded: {{uploaded}} of {{total}} runs uploaded – date, bytes, section count
account.sync.failed.settingsRead: Your account’s settings could not be read, so this machine keeps its own. windowsweep tries again the next time it starts.
account.sync.failed.settingsWrite: Your latest settings have not reached your account. On this machine they stay exactly as they are, and windowsweep tries again the next time it starts.
account.sync.failed.upload_one: One run summary has not reached your account. windowsweep keeps it on this machine and tries again the next time it starts.
account.sync.failed.upload_other: {{count}} run summaries have not reached your account. windowsweep keeps them on this machine and tries again the next time it starts.
account.sync.failed.list: The run summaries in your account could not be read. Nothing on this machine changed, and windowsweep tries again the next time you open this screen.
account.sync.failed.listMore: The next page could not be read; nothing on this machine changed. Press again to retry.
account.sync.failed.remove: windowsweep could not confirm that this run summary was removed, so it stays in the list. Nothing on this machine changed, and you can press Remove again.
account.sync.conflict.notice: Your account held newer settings, so they replaced this machine’s.
account.disagree.summary: What happens when two machines disagree
account.disagree.settings: The newer change wins, and this screen tells you which one it was, with an <1>Undo</1> that puts the other back. Settings are small and rarely edited on two machines at once, so a silent merge would be more surprising than a visible choice.
account.disagree.runs: Run history never conflicts: a run belongs to the machine that made it and is only ever added or removed, never edited.
account.runs.title: Run summaries
account.runs.removeNote: Remove deletes one run’s summary from your account; it touches no log or report on this machine or any other. There is no undo.
account.runs.empty: Your account holds no run summaries. When a run finishes in the desktop app on any machine signed in as you, its summary appears here; runs from before you signed in stay on this machine.
account.signOutNote: Signing out clears every local trace of the account, including the rows cached from your other machines.
account.notConfigured: Sign-in is not configured in this build
account.notConfiguredNote: The OAuth client id is absent, so this build cannot sign in. Everything else works exactly the same.
account.deleteWhatGoes: This removes the account itself, its profile, the settings it synced, the summary of every run it holds, and any contact requests you sent us. It happens the moment you press the button, and there is no undo.
account.deleteWhatStays: Nothing on this PC is touched. windowsweep deletes no local files here – your reports, your local history and every cleanup feature stay exactly as they are, and all of it keeps working signed out.
account.deleteConfirmLabel: Type <1>{{word}}</1> to confirm. It must match exactly.
account.deleteDone: Your account is gone, and you are signed out here. Nothing on this PC changed.
